title: The earth
hook: why some Hindus ask the earth's pardon before their feet touch the floor: the Prithvi Sukta and the earth as a shared mother
tomorrow: two schools argued over what to sing to a bride. who won?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: the poor. Martin cut his cloak in two and met Christ in a beggar at the gate. Today, the ground under that gate.

An alarm. A phone already in hand. Feet on the floor before the eyes are fully open. Some Hindus pause right there. Before their feet touch the ground, they say a short Sanskrit verse to the earth, and it ends with an apology: forgive me for touching you with my feet. Saying sorry to a floor. That's the odd detail. Why would anyone ask the ground's pardon for standing on it?
screen: `AN ALARM, A PHONE, FEET ON THE FLOOR.` → `A VERSE BEFORE THE FIRST STEP.` → `FORGIVE ME FOR TOUCHING YOU.`

segments.voice: The verse is a traditional morning prayer, and it speaks to the earth as a goddess: clothed in the oceans, the wife of Vishnu. Hindus call her Bhudevi. Nobody can live without stepping on her, so you greet her first and ask her pardon. And the idea has a scripture behind it. The Atharva Veda has a long hymn to the earth, the Prithvi Sukta. In one verse the singer says the earth is his mother and he is her son. In another, the earth carries people of many languages and many customs, each in their own home. So here's the puzzle solved. In this Hindu teaching, the earth isn't a backdrop, and she isn't simply property. She's a mother you live on, and everyone else lives on her too. You don't trash your mother's house, and you aren't her only child. One to tell a friend tonight: some classical Indian dancers touch the floor before they dance, asking the earth's pardon for the stamping to come. A pope, writing as a Christian, reached for a close picture. Pope Francis subtitled his letter on the environment: on care for our common home.
screen: `BHUDEVI, CLOTHED IN THE OCEANS.` · `THE EARTH IS MY MOTHER.` · `MANY LANGUAGES, ONE EARTH.` · `DANCERS ASK HER PARDON.` · then, large: `THE COMMON HOME.`

segments.voice: Put your palm flat on the floor, or on the ground if you're outside. Feel that it's holding you up right now, and holding everyone else too. Keep your hand there while you breathe, and choose one thing you'll stop throwing away this week.
The earth: in Hindu teaching, Bhudevi, a mother who carries people of every language. The floor under you is her house, and theirs.
Keep this: the common home, one earth carrying everyone, greeted with an apology each morning. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Hindus say a short Sanskrit morning verse to the earth (Samudra vasane devi) before stepping out of bed, touching the ground and then their forehead. The Prithvi Sukta of the Atharva Veda is recited as a hymn to the earth.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3: written new in recipe v3, shape puzzle. Puzzle: why some Hindus ask the earth's pardon each morning. Teaching named: the earth as Bhudevi, a mother who carries all peoples (Atharva Veda 12.1, the Prithvi Sukta). The phrase 'common home' is credited to Pope Francis's Laudato si' subtitle.

Check: the morning verse is traditional (not from one scripture) and is said by some Hindus, hedged as 'some'. The verse addresses the earth as ocean-clothed and wife of Vishnu; the line about mountains is left out. 'Some classical Indian dancers touch the floor before they dance' (bhumi pranam in Bharatanatyam and other forms) is hedged; confirm. Verse numbers 12 and 45 of AV 12.1 follow the Shaunaka recension; confirm.
